cultura.name: El Arpa Paraguaya
cultura.description:
The diatonic harp is Paraguay's national instrument, played with bare fingers.
Its warm, rolling sound defines guarania — Paraguay's signature musical genre.

cultura.name: El Idioma Guaraní
cultura.description:
Paraguay is the only South American country where an indigenous language is co-official.
Over 90% of Paraguayans speak Guaraní — woven into everyday speech and identity.

cultura.name: El Ñandutí
cultura.description:
Intricate spider-web lace crafted by hand in dazzling concentric patterns.
The word ñandutí means 'spider web' in Guaraní — worn as collars, shawls, and art.

cultura.name: Las Misiones Jesuíticas
cultura.description:
17th–18th century Jesuit reductions built thriving communities of Guaraní peoples.
UNESCO-listed ruins at Trinidad and Jesús remain spiritual and architectural wonders.

india_traveller.visa_note: Indian passport holders do not require a tourist visa for Paraguay for stays up to 90 days. This makes Paraguay one of the easier South American destinations. Ensure your passport is valid for at least 6 months beyond your travel date.
india_traveller.flight_note: No direct or single-stop flights from India to Paraguay. Common routes go via São Paulo (GRU) or Buenos Aires (EZE) on LATAM, Qatar Airways + LATAM, or similar combinations. Total journey time is typically 22–28 hours. Asunción's Silvio Pettirossi Airport (ASU) is the main entry point.
india_traveller.cost_per_day_inr: Paraguay is one of South America's most affordable countries. Budget travellers can manage on ₹1,800–3,000/day. Mid-range travel costs around ₹4,000–7,000/day. The guaraní has weakened significantly, making street food, transport, and accommodation very cheap by Indian standards.
india_traveller.veg_tips: Paraguay is a heavily meat-based cuisine, so vegetarians need to plan ahead. Safe bets are sopa paraguaya (corn bread), chipá (cheese bread), mbejú (starch flatbread), and rice-and-vegetable dishes. In Asunción, look for international restaurants. Always say: 'Soy vegetariano/a, sin carne ni pollo, por favor.'
